correctness.rationale: Complete leading-eigenvalue resolvent equation has a unique positive spectral root above the shifted first Dirichlet pole; the Laplace survival kernel excludes higher nonreal spectrum. Explicit Green curvature in squared reset destination switches strict convexity at resolvent parameter zero, proving all-width convex-order sign reversal at sqrt(m2+2/r). The Dirichlet perturbation expansion proves the fourth-moment coefficient. Standalone Fraction interval arithmetic certifies all four strict extinction/growth signs for one habitat and two rates.

value.rationale: A recent fixed-return-site critical-habitat study directly proposes distributed resetting, making its distributional robustness a motivated gap. The theorem gives a sharp comparison across all compact reset-site distributions under a natural fixed-second-moment budget; the exact same-habitat extinction-versus-growth reversal shows the structural effect changes an ecological threshold, not just a parameterized formula. The fourth-moment coefficient quantifies the boundary near the critical resetting rate without overstating nonlinear or stochastic consequences.
